findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add (to 271c or 3388) a corpus echo-safety test that runs ≥5 repeated render/decode passes over the DC corpus and asserts no monotonic length decay (incl. the ASCII-table ratchet body), matching parent AC2's terms.
evidence: Parent AC2: '... echo-safe with zero content erosion over ≥5 repeated passes, including the known ASCII-table ratchet body; verified by a corpus echo-safety test asserting no monotonic length decay.'

271c AC: 'ASCII tables are verbatim-wrapped in {noformat} and do not erode across passes; verified by test_dc_table_noformat_stable over the 70 known erosion bodies (70/70 stable)' — no ≥5-pass count, no monotonic-length-decay assertion, and scoped to table bodies only.
3388 AC: 'After the DC cutover ... a second pass emits zero description updates' — two passes.
3289 AC: 'state-based echo-safety across a second pass' — two passes.
findings.finding: Parent AC2 requires DC echo-safety with 'zero content erosion over ≥5 repeated passes ... verified by a corpus echo-safety test asserting no monotonic length decay,' but no sibling delivers that specific observable: 271c asserts only table stability ('70/70 stable', 'do not erode across passes') with no ≥5-pass count and no monotonic-length-decay metric, while 3388 (test_dc_cutover_converges) and 3289 (live) assert only a SECOND pass.
scenarios: A DC body that is echo-stable across 2 passes but slowly erodes over 5+ passes (the multi-pass ratchet the corpus test is meant to catch) passes every sibling test yet violates parent AC2.
The completion verifier looks for a corpus echo-safety test asserting no monotonic length decay over ≥5 passes and finds none named in any child.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend 271c's table/coverage tests (or 3388's DC convergence tests) with an explicit ≥5-pass corpus loop asserting non-decreasing (no monotonic decay) body length, so the parent's exact metric is measured.

findings.finding: Parent AC4 specifies verification 'by the concurrent-conflict regression test over the corpus (the proven 799/799-detected invariant),' but the covering siblings verify the behavior without the same-terms corpus measurement: 3388's test_concurrent_conflict_alerts and 3289's live test both assert local-wins + conflict-alert on a single/both-sides edit, neither asserting the 799/799 corpus-wide detection count.
scenarios: A subset of the 799 known concurrent-conflict corpus cases fails detection while the single-scenario unit/live tests still pass — the corpus-wide 799/799 invariant AC4 names is never measured.
findings.suggested_fix: In 3388, add a corpus-driven concurrent-conflict regression asserting all 799 known both-sides cases raise the outbound-field-conflict alert (799/799), alongside the existing single-scenario test_concurrent_conflict_alerts.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify DC behavior on platforms with no pypandoc-binary build (e.g. BSD): either surface a clear degraded-mode signal or document that the wiki-render feature is a no-op there, so it doesn't silently regress to literal-Markdown output.
evidence: 'render structurally-safe units to wiki via pinned pypandoc-binary ... identity-passthrough fallback when pandoc is absent'
pypandoc-binary distributes prebuilt pandoc only for Linux/macOS/Windows; BSD is a supported platform in the rebar matrix with no wheel
findings.finding: The DC wiki renderer depends on a bundled `pypandoc-binary`. pypandoc-binary ships prebuilt pandoc wheels for Linux/macOS/Windows but not for BSD. On a BSD platform the bundled binary is absent, so the plan's own 'identity-passthrough fallback when pandoc is absent' triggers and DC bodies are sent as literal Markdown source — the exact defect this feature sets out to fix — silently, only on that platform.
findings.location: Child responsibilities — 'DC wiki renderer'; 'render structurally-safe units to wiki via pinned pypandoc-binary ... identity-passthrough fallback when pandoc is absent'
scenarios: Platform=BSD, Target=any, DC Jira target: pypandoc-binary provides no BSD pandoc build, renderer falls back to identity, and DC descriptions/comments display raw Markdown (`## heading`, `- [ ]`) instead of wiki markup — the user observes unrendered source with no error.
findings.suggested_fix: State the platform coverage of the bundled pandoc explicitly and, where absent, emit a diagnostic (log/warning) rather than a silent identity fallback so operators know rendering is disabled.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly that DC's WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound changes from identity to decode_inbound(to_wire(t)) at cutover, and require the child to re-assert the pinned normalize_outbound(t)==decode_inbound(to_wire(t)) law over the lossy renderer (including the verbatim-passthrough units), so the description differ and comment diff stay convergent through the port-compare layer, not only through the ADR-0026 baseline.
evidence: outbound_comments.py:44-56 documents the load-bearing invariant 'RichTextCodec.normalize_outbound(t) == RichTextCodec.decode_inbound(RichTextCodec.to_wire(t))' and states 'If that law ever stops holding ... a body pulled FROM Jira starts being re-emitted on the next outbound pass, silently overwriting the human's Jira-native formatting'
outbound_comments.py:401 'compare_body = codec.normalize_outbound(sanitizer.fit_comment(body))' compared against decode_inbound-produced jira_bodies
outbound_mapper.py:76-77 and backend.py:49-50 make the description compare value normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(value)) — a codec fixed point today

rich_text.py:96-108: DC's WikiTextCodec currently makes to_wire/decode_inbound/normalize_outbound all identity, so the law is trivially satisfied; a lossy to_wire (MD->wiki render) breaks it unless normalize_outbound is co-changed AND decode_inbound(render(t)) is genuinely idempotent over the 'dangerous units passed verbatim' path
test_rich_text_codec.py::test_normalize_outbound_equals_decode_of_to_wire pins this law (per outbound_comments.py:50)
findings.finding: The DC cutover redefines WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound from its current identity (rich_text.py:96-98) to decode_inbound(to_wire(t)), but the plan does not flag that this is a behavior change to a currently-closed contract nor that it must keep satisfying the pinned echo-safety law normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t)) — a law that today holds trivially (all three ops identity) and is depended on by both the description differ and the comment diff.
findings.location: Approach / 'Live cutover + state echo suppression' child ('DC: to_wire->renderer and normalize_outbound->decode_inbound(to_wire(t))')
scenarios: A DC description whose 'structurally-safe' units render to wiki but whose verbatim-passed-through units (ASCII tables in {noformat}, prose arrows) do not re-decode to the same normalized string, so normalize_outbound != decode_inbound(to_wire(...)) and the port-level description differ re-emits on every pass before the baseline suppresses it
A comment body on DC where the comment-diff compare key (normalize_outbound) no longer equals the decoded Jira body, re-emitting an 'add' each pass
findings.suggested_fix: In the state-echo-suppression child, add an explicit note that DC normalize_outbound is redefined to decode_inbound(to_wire(t)) and add an acceptance check that test_normalize_outbound_equals_decode_of_to_wire (and its comment-path analogue) still passes for WikiTextCodec once to_wire renders MD->wiki, covering a body that mixes structurally-safe and verbatim-passthrough units.
